title: Where the Oversize Comes From, Explained
subtitle: Ragnhild Uzoma and Brynjar Obiora on tracing quarry boulders to the uncharged top of the bench
summary: A research explainer from the School of Underlying Conditions on Ragnhild Uzoma and Brynjar Obiora's study of the oversize from three dolerite bench blasts. It follows the colour-banded grout from the marker holes to the boulders that carry it, then sets the result beside the drill's own record of the ground. Uzoma and Obiora describe the work in their own words.
topic: A research explainer of the paper tracing oversize boulders in a dolerite quarry bench to the uncharged stemming zone of their blastholes, by depth-banded grout in marker holes and the drill's own penetration-rate record

beats.text: Where in the bench was each boulder standing before the blast?

A boulder that formed across a marker hole carries a half-barrel or full barrel of grout on one face. Its colour, or the boundary between two colours where a boulder spanned a lift contact, gives the boulder’s depth of origin to the metre.

beats.text: The ground that yields most of the oversize is the ground the drill describes most closely, and the charge never reaches.
A core logger learns early to write down what didn’t come up. This study let us do the same for what did.
